candidate_targets: lack of clarity in personal values
original_extraction.evidence_text:
Many of the concepts in ACT closely resemble those from many religions, particularly the idea of
living life according to your values. But whereas most religions prescribe a ready-made set of
values for you, ACT asks you to clarify and connect with your own values. Moreover, ACT does
not encourage you to adopt any particular belief system. (Thus, my frequent advice throughout this
book: ‘Don’t believe something just because I say so—trust your own experience.’) ACT takes the
view that if your beliefs work to enrich your life, then that’s all that matters.

---

People often see similarities between ACT and Buddhism: both emphasise the practice of
mindfulness; both encourage living by your values; both share the assumption that psychological
suffering is a universal human phenomenon, created by the natural processes of the normal human
mind; and both assume that our commonsense attempts to find happiness and avoid pain frequently
lead only to more pain. As Steven Hayes puts it: ‘The large overlap between ACT and Buddhism is
remarkable, considering that the former is based on principles of behaviour therapy and the second
is embedded in a spiritual and religious tradition that spans thousands of years.’
generation_rules: Do not adopt ready-made values; clarify and connect with personal values; trust personal experience over external authority; practice mindfulness regularly.
original_extraction.psychological_function: Reduce psychological suffering by accepting it as a universal human phenomenon; promote living according to self-chosen values rather than prescribed beliefs; encourage experiential trust over imposed beliefs.
repetition_rules: Frequent advice to 'Don’t believe something just because I say so—trust your own experience.'
original_extraction.therapeutic_function: Clarify and connect with one's own values to enrich life; practice mindfulness to address psychological suffering; recognize that attempts to find happiness and avoid pain can lead to more pain.
voice_rules: Encourage a non-dogmatic, experiential voice; avoid prescribing beliefs; promote self-trust and personal validation.
